A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PipeFusion research. All pages, including equations, figures, tables and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original Pixart experiments measuring latency, memory, FID and LPIPS, together with patch-count, warmup and interconnect analyses.

after.justification: V3 reports original latency and memory experiments on Pixart, SD3 and Flux.1, FID evaluations on Pixart and Flux.1, and scalability and warmup analyses.

M1.justification: The patch partitioning, layer pipeline, stale-KV reuse and asynchronous P2P procedure are retained. V3 Section 4.2 adds implemented classifier-free-guidance parallelism combined with PipeFusion, dividing GPUs between conditional and unconditional passes. This is a limited extension of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate caption-conditioned image generation, retain COCO Captions 2014 for quality evaluation, and include high-resolution tests up to 8192px. Adding SD3 and Flux changes model configurations within this coverage; the revised sampling, preprocessing and hardware belong to experimental settings.

E2.justification: V3 actually benchmarks hybrid Ulysses/Ring configurations through USP, which v1 only discusses. The scalability comparison also expands from PipeFusion and DistriFusion in v1 Figure 10a to include tensor parallelism and tuned sequence parallelism for Pixart in v3 Figure 8, substantially broadening the central comparisons.

E3.justification: V1's A100/L20 experiments are replaced by L40 experiments, including new 2B SD3 and 12B Flux configurations. V3 explicitly excludes VAE decoding from latency, whereas v1 describes end-to-end timing. Quality evaluation changes from 5,000 images and four warmup steps to 30,000 images and one warmup step, adds FID against serial outputs, and removes LPIPS evaluation.

E4.justification: The patch-count analysis is revised and explicitly excludes warmup in v3 Figure 12; new Table 2 measures warmup latency across three models. V1's controlled PCIe/NVLink comparison, consecutive-input similarity visualization, and warmup image-quality/LPIPS analysis are removed. These changes substantially alter the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: V3 Section 4.2 newly states that latency figures average five runs; v1 provides no repetition count. This establishes additional reporting, not an increase in runs. Neither version supplies confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V3 replaces hardware-specific latency and memory results and adds SD3, Flux and CFG-hybrid results. Figure 10 newly reports Flux memory of 10.89/12.34 GB for PipeFusion versus 33.86/34.07 GB for sequence parallelism at 1024/2048px. Pixart's serial-reference ground-truth FID changes from 30.89 to 22.78, but the changed evaluation protocol prevents interpreting this as a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Table 1 changes Ulysses communication from 4O(p*hs)L to (4/N)O(p*hs)L, supplies the previously missing Ring cost, and revises PipeFusion's cache-memory dependence from patch count M to device count N. V3 Section 3.5 adds collective-communication factors and the N < 2L condition. These materially revise the cost analysis; the pipeline-utilization formula remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The central communication- and memory-efficient pipeline contribution persists. V3 adds an explicit state-of-the-art latency claim for three named models on L40 GPUs and emphasizes large-parameter Flux applicability. V1's explicit PCIe/NVLink parity and operational-cost claims are no longer retained.

C2.justification: V1 reports visibly inferior quality with zero or one warmup step and near-original results with four; v3 instead emphasizes model dependence and satisfactory Pixart generation without warmup using zero-initialized KV buffers. V3 also adds SD3 positional-encoding limitations and Flux parameter-versus-activation memory tradeoffs, while dropping the earlier NVLink and uneven-layer-partitioning qualifications.

D1.justification: The code access location changes from PipeFusion/PipeFusion to xdit-project/xDiT. V3 updates PyTorch/diffusers versions, specifies CUDA and Clean-FID, and documents SD3/Flux variants and schedulers. V1's FlashAttention version and VAE convolution-chunking details are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: V3 explicitly positions PipeFusion as adapting TeraPipe's sequence pipeline through temporal redundancy, explaining the causal-versus-full-attention distinction. Related work substantially expands to temporal caching approaches such as DeepCache, Delta-DiT, PAB and DiTFastAttn, while earlier batch-pipeline and sampling/distillation discussions and citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related work are extensively rewritten. Tensor and sequence parallelism receive separate subsections, a comparative-analysis subsection is introduced, and quality results and ablations move from experimental subsections into standalone Sections 5 and 6. The title, terminology and author header also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout with extensive visual redesign. Method diagrams add the inference workflow, Ulysses comparison, explicit layer partitioning and a DistriFusion freshness panel. Performance plots are replaced, the quality grid gains an embedded FID table, Table 1 is restructured, and a warmup table is added.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's Pixart-only study, v3 better supports parameter-sharding benefits through large-model memory results, stronger USP comparisons, revised cost analysis and clearer TeraPipe attribution. These gains are tempered by removing interconnect and warmup-quality controls and by internal reporting inconsistencies: SD3 CFG speedups disagree with Figure 6, and Flux USP configurations differ between prose and Figure 7.
